source_title: Hydrodynamic limits for kinetic equations preserving mass, momentum and energy: a spectral and unified approach in the presence of a spectral gap
title: Strong Navier–Stokes–Fourier hydrodynamic limits with kinetic and acoustic layers under symmetric and nonsymmetric collision bounds
core_obligations: Assuming the spectral theorem and cited NSF Cauchy/heat/wave/paraproduct inputs, the stiff epsilon^-1 quadratic term is not directly controlled in a single uniform-in-time norm. The author constructs coupled kinetic/mixed/hydrodynamic unknowns in different velocity and dissipation spaces, removes the acoustic initial layer, uses an NSF-solution-dependent time weight and a hierarchy epsilon<<c3<<eta<<c2 to close the nonlinear source/contraction estimates, and proves convergence and uniqueness on the given fluid lifespan. Under the nonsymmetric BED estimates a modified Picard scheme and a semigroup-defined kinetic dissipative inner product close the hierarchy; convergence is in the weaker space using stronger stability. This is the one complete H3 hydrodynamic-limit problem with its BE/BED author branches,not separate counts for the Picard estimate or for rewriting the same limit in different spaces.
